summary: The Internet & Television Association (NCTA) supports maintaining the current E-Rate program, but suggests improvements such as increasing consultant oversight and adding controls for MIBS. NCTA opposes narrowing the eligibility scope of E-Rate to reduce costs. The FCC should reject proposals to sunset the E-Rate program and maintain its availability nationwide to ensure connectivity for schools and libraries. The FCC should increase oversight of consultants in the E-Rate program and consider other modifications to bolster program integrity. The E-Rate program supports the mission of connecting schools and libraries. The FCC should reject suggestions to make harmful structural changes to the program and instead focus on proposals that improve its integrity and efficiency.
